tutorial.title: App Tutorial
tutorial.subtitle: Learn how to use the Product Importer
tutorial.description: This tutorial will guide you step by step through all the app's features. We'll go through each section in order, explaining what it does and how to configure it.
tutorial.sectionsDescription: The tutorial covers the following sections in order:
tutorial.tipReactive: You can re-enable the tutorial at any time from the "Tutorial" button in the side menu.
tutorial.tipNavigation: Use the "Next" and "Previous" buttons to navigate between steps in each section.
tutorial.tipAutoAdvance: When you finish a section, the tutorial automatically advances to the next one.
tutorial.tipExit: Click "Exit" at any time to stop the tutorial.
tutorial.dashboardDescription: This is your main screen where you'll see all your configured suppliers. Each supplier has its own data file (CSV or Excel) with the products you want to import to your Shopify store.
tutorial.newSupplierDescription: Click here to create a new supplier. You'll be asked for a name (you can use any name you like), and then you can configure its CSV/Excel file, price rules, column mapping, and more.
tutorial.supplierListDescription: Here you'll see all your suppliers. Use 'New supplier' at the top right to add a new one. Each supplier shows its name, status (Active/Inactive), number of products, import mode, and last import.
tutorial.configureSupplierDescription: This button takes you to the full supplier configuration: data source, column mapping, price rules, category mapping, and import.
tutorial.importHistoryDescription: Here you can see all past imports for this supplier: when they ran, how many products were created or updated, and if there were any errors.
tutorial.deleteSupplierDescription: Deletes the supplier and all its configuration. Products already created in Shopify will NOT be deleted; only the import configuration is lost.
tutorial.supplierTabsDescription: Each supplier has 7 tabs: Import, Configuration, Columns, Price Rules, Categories, Preview, and History. We'll explore each one.
tutorial.dataSourceDescription: Here you define where your product file comes from. You can use a remote URL (automatic updates) or upload a local CSV/Excel file. The URL will be refreshed on each scheduled import.
tutorial.remoteModeDescription: Select this option if your provider offers a direct link to the file (CSV or Excel). The system will automatically download the file on each import.
tutorial.delimiterDescription: If your file uses a separator other than comma (e.g., pipe | or semicolon ;), select it here. 'Auto' detects the delimiter automatically. Only applies to CSV files.
tutorial.frequencyDescription: Defines how often the automatic import will run. From 30 minutes to weekly. Only available with remote URL.
tutorial.productStatusDescription: When a new product is created, it will be published as Draft (visible only to you) or Active (visible to customers). Existing products keep their current status.
tutorial.importModeDescription: Chunks: imports products in small batches, slower but with progress preview. Bulk: uses Shopify's Bulk Operations, much faster for large catalogs.
tutorial.batchSizeDescription: Number processed per batch in Chunks mode. A larger size is faster but uses more memory. Maximum 250. Only applies in Chunks mode.
tutorial.retriesDescription: If a product fails to import, it will be retried this many times before being skipped. Useful if the Shopify API has temporary rate limits. Maximum 10.
tutorial.updateFieldsDescription: Select which fields will be updated on products that already exist in Shopify. For example, you can choose to update price and stock but NOT name or description.
tutorial.defaultTagsDescription: Tags that will be added to ALL imported products. Separate multiple tags with commas. These tags are combined with the specific tags for each category.
tutorial.salesChannelsDescription: Select which channels products will be published to: Online Store, Point of Sale, etc. Existing products are not modified.
tutorial.exclusionsDescription: Define rules to skip products: by title words (e.g., outlet, refurbished), by SKU pattern (e.g., OUT-*), or by EAN. You can also skip specific fields (price, stock) by SKU.
tutorial.inventoryLocationDescription: Select the Shopify location where stock will be updated. If you have multiple warehouses, choose which one to use for this supplier.
tutorial.columnMappingDescription: Here you connect the columns from your file (CSV or Excel) with Shopify fields. For example: the 'name' column from the file → 'Title' field in Shopify. If you don't map a field, the default value will be used if you define one.
tutorial.selectColumnDescription: In each dropdown you'll see all columns detected in your file. Select the column that corresponds to each Shopify field. If a field doesn't exist in your file, leave it as '— Don't map —'.
tutorial.defaultValueDescription: If a field isn't in your file, you can define a fixed value here. For example, if your file doesn't have a brand column, type the default brand in this field.
tutorial.priceRulesDescription: Define how the selling price of your products is calculated. You can create formulas like 'C*1.262' (cost × 1.262) or 'C+5' (cost + 5€). Formulas use C = supplier cost.
tutorial.ruleTypeDescription: General: applies to all products. By category: applies only to products in specific categories. By SKU: applies to specific products. The priority is: SKU > Category > General.
tutorial.priceFormulaDescription: Write the formula to calculate the price. Variables: C = supplier cost. Operators: *, +, -, /, parentheses. Examples: C*1.25 (with margin), C+10 (fixed margin), (C*1.5)/1.21.
tutorial.roundingDescription: Rounds the calculated price to .95, .99, or a custom value (e.g., .90). Useful for psychological pricing. Example: 19.97€ is rounded to 19.95€.
tutorial.compareAtDescription: The strikethrough price customers see. It can be a formula (e.g., C*2), a fixed value added to cost, or a percentage of cost. It shows as 'from X€' in the store.
tutorial.priceRangesDescription: For general and category rules, you can enable ranges. This allows different formulas based on the product's cost. Example: if C < 10 → C*2, if C >= 10 → C*1.5.
tutorial.existingRulesDescription: All created rules are organized by type: General, By Category, and By SKU. You can enable/disable, edit, preview, or delete each rule.
tutorial.categoryMappingDescription: Connect the categories from your file (CSV or Excel) with Shopify collections. For example: the 'Electronics' category from the file → 'Technology' collection in your store.
tutorial.fileCategoriesDescription: Search and select the file categories you want to map. The system automatically loads all categories detected in the file.
tutorial.shopifyCollectionsDescription: Select one or more Shopify collections where products from this category will be added. A product can belong to multiple collections.
tutorial.tagsPerCategoryDescription: Specific tags that will be added only to products in this category. They are combined with the default tags configured in Settings.
tutorial.shopifyTypeDescription: Assign a specific Shopify product type for this category. If you don't select one, the type configured in column mapping will be used.
tutorial.importPreviewDescription: Before importing, you can see a preview of which products will be created, updated, or skipped. This helps you verify that the configuration is correct.
tutorial.previewFiltersDescription: Filter the preview by: all products, individual SKUs, or specific categories. Useful for reviewing just a portion of the catalog.
tutorial.previewStatsDescription: Quick summary: how many rows the file has, how many products were filtered, how many will be created, updated, already up to date, or excluded by exclusion rules.
tutorial.productTableDescription: Each row shows: SKU, name, action (CREATE/UPDATE/SKIP), cost, calculated price, comparison price, stock in file vs Shopify, category, and errors if any.
tutorial.productActionsDescription: CREATE (green): new product that will be created. UPDATE (yellow): existing product that will be updated. SKIP: will be skipped. EXCLUDED: matches exclusion rules. NO CHANGES: identical data.
tutorial.importButtonDescription: Click to launch the import. If another is in progress, it will be added to the queue. The button changes to 'Enqueue import' when there's an active import.
tutorial.importFiltersDescription: Limit the import to specific SKUs or categories. If you don't select anything, all products from the file are imported.
tutorial.lastImportStatsDescription: Summary of the most recent import: mapped products, created, updated, errors, and excluded.
tutorial.scheduledImportDescription: Enable or disable automatic importing. When active, the system downloads and processes the file automatically according to the configured frequency.
tutorial.quickActionsDescription: Shortcuts to navigate to other supplier sections: Preview, Configuration, Columns, Price Rules, and Categories.
tutorial.historyTabDescription: Here you can see all past imports for this supplier: when they ran, how many products were created or updated, and if there were any errors.
tutorial.historyDescription: Table with the record of each import: date, mode (chunks/bulk), products processed, created, updated, unchanged, price changes, stock changes, errors, and status. Up to 100 records are stored; older ones are automatically deleted.
tutorial.historyFullDescription: Complete record of this supplier's imports. A maximum of 100 records are stored; older ones are automatically deleted when a new import completes.
tutorial.historyTableDescription: Each row is an import: start and end date, status (completed/error), trigger (manual/cron/webhook), total products, created, updated, unchanged, price changes, stock changes, and errors.
tutorial.settingsDescription: Global settings that affect all suppliers in your store. Here you define what happens when two suppliers import the same product.
tutorial.duplicatePolicyDescription: Create both: allows duplicates (two products with the same EAN). Prioritize supplier: the supplier with higher priority replaces the other. Skip if already exists: the duplicate product is skipped.
tutorial.supplierPriorityDescription: Order suppliers from highest to lowest priority. When a duplicate is detected and the policy is 'Prioritize', the supplier with higher priority wins. Use the arrows ↑↓ to reorder.
tutorial.duplicatesDescription: This is where products with the same EAN but different SKU from two suppliers appear. You can mark them as resolved to ignore them.
tutorial.duplicatesTableDescription: Each row shows a pair of products with the same EAN from two different suppliers: the EAN, supplier A and its SKU, supplier B and its SKU, when it was detected, and whether it's resolved or not. If more suppliers have the same EAN, more pairs are generated.
tutorial.queueDescription: Monitor all imports in progress and queued. If you launch several imports at once, they are processed in order. You can cancel any import from here.
tutorial.runningImports: The imports currently running. Shows progress, last SKU processed, and errors if any. You can cancel them with the red button.
tutorial.recentImportsDescription: Last 10 imports from all suppliers: manual and scheduled (cron). Updates automatically. For the full history of each supplier, go to its History tab.
